_comment: Panel-of-judges pipeline config. Credentials are ENV VAR NAMES, never values; keys live in the environment or a gitignored .env next to the harness.
routing_comment: `provider`/`id` is the native route and stays the default. The optional `openrouter` block is a fallback harness.resolve() takes only when the native key is absent; tags and panel membership are unchanged either way, and metrics.jsonl records the id actually called. OpenRouter has no Batch API, so a fallback-routed tag must run realtime. Mirror ids and prices are hand-maintained against openrouter.ai/api/v1/models and nothing checks them -- re-verify before trusting a cost estimate.

panels._frontier_fast_note: Calibration panel: deepseek holds the third seat instead of kimi, because K3 spends 8-18 minutes and 25-57k reasoning tokens on a whole-doc call. glm is the designated substitute if deepseek fails. The audition data behind that choice lives with the calibration runlogs in experiments/panel-calibration/, not here. Production frontier/frontier_primary are unaffected.
panels._comment: frontier = every tag whose rows the site builder may admit (primaries AND substitutes). frontier_primary = the judges the run driver executes; substitutes (opus, kimi-k2) are run manually per Skill 4 when a primary fails.
panels._itest_note: single cheap judge for end-to-end integration testing (~2 cents per behaviour); never for published data. Must be a long-context model: whole-doc prompts reach ~65k tokens (qwen-small's 41k context cannot fit them).

param_quirks_comment: gpt-5*: max_completion_tokens + reasoning_effort (gpt-5.6: low, else minimal), no temperature. fable/mythos: no temperature. others: temperature=0.

display._comment: Behaviours shown in site/llm-panel-review (build_site_data.py): `behaviours` is the sidebar list, `panel` selects which config panel's runlog rows the builder admits. `threshold` and `solid_threshold` are read by build_site_data.py but neither controls what the page renders: applyPanelThreshold() in site/llm-panel-review/app.js recomputes every citation's score from its baked per-judge verdicts on load and on every tier toggle, then derives the band from the per-cell judge count. `threshold` appears only in the builder's closing summary; `solid_threshold` is baked into each citation as `adjacent`, which the reader overwrites on load, so the baked flag is not what you see. Legacy URL params: ?threshold= maps to tier bands once at load, ?solid= is stripped and ignored. The band cuts live with tierBand() and bandReachable() in app.js and are pinned by engine/panel/test_appjs_tiers.js -- read them there, not from a line number here.
display._generated_note: Curated panel-review display list (registry reader-test slugs), hand-maintained; engine/panel/build_site_data.py validates every entry against data/behaviours.json, so a renamed or unknown slug fails the build.
display._activation_note: The two general-guidelines slugs (animal-welfare-impacts, general-welfare-impacts-strict) join this list when the full rollout data lands; until then the dual-slug mapping in build_site_data.py is inert by design.

_opus_note: Substitution: opus stands in for fable on harm-avoidance-to-third-parties x model-spec, and only there; opus rows exist for no other cell. Why, and the matching kimi-k2 substitution, are recorded in SUBSTITUTION_NOTES in engine/panel/build_site_data.py, which is what puts them in the payload.
